<a id="LeadingLegOf"></a>

### Where the leading leg goes

`LeadingLegOf` · `src/content.ts:93` · status: **held**

In a pose that sets the legs apart, reached from a level above (standing, folded), the leading leg steps back; reached from the floor (a plank, a dog), it comes forward between the hands.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
() => (before: Level): Stance => (before === Level.standing || before === Level.fold ? Stance.back : Stance.front)
```

</details>

<a id="MakesSense"></a>

### A sequence that makes sense

`MakesSense` · `src/content.ts:117` · status: **held**

The poses of a sequence, judged by their level: it begins standing and ends standing; each pose is at the level of the one before or at a level a body reaches from it in one movement; it does not go back and forth between two levels twice in a row (standing, folding, standing, folding); no pose follows itself. It gives what is wrong: whether it begins and ends standing, where it jumps, where it goes back and forth once too often, where a pose repeats.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
({ ways, counts, seq }) => (steps: readonly { id: string; level: Level }[]): { begins: boolean; ends: boolean; jumps: number[]; backAndForth: number[]; repeats: number[] } => {
    const levels = steps.map((p) => p.level)
    const { previous, zero } = counts
    return {
      begins: seq.head(levels) === Level.standing,
      ends: seq.last(levels) === Level.standing,
      jumps: levels.flatMap((l, i) => {
        const before = levels.at(previous(i))
        return i > zero && before !== undefined && l !== before && !ways[before].includes(l) ? [i] : []
      }),
      backAndForth: levels.flatMap((l, i) => {
        const [one, two, three] = [previous(i), previous(previous(i)), previous(previous(previous(i)))]
        return three >= zero && l === levels.at(two) && levels.at(one) === levels.at(three) && l !== levels.at(one) ? [i] : []
      }),
      repeats: steps.flatMap((p, i) => (i > zero && p.id === steps.at(previous(i))?.id ? [i] : [])),
    }
  }
```

</details>

- Owner: ghalaax
- Parameters: `ways` ← [The ways between levels](#LevelWays) · `counts` ← [Counts](../.trame/std/docs/algebra.md#Counts) · `seq` ← [Sequences](../.trame/std/docs/algebra.md#Sequences)
- Refines: [Practise yoga on one's own, guided](product.md#PractiseGuided)
- Used by: [The composer](composing.md#ComposerViewOf), [A sequence drawn by lot](composing.md#DrawnSequence), [Sequences drawn by lot](scenarios.md#DrawnSequencesMakeSense)
- Verified by: [Sequences drawn by lot](scenarios.md#DrawnSequencesMakeSense)
- Used by: [Sequences](#Sequences)

**Criteria of a sequence that makes sense · owner: ghalaax**

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| The sun salutation makes sense | passed |
| Standing then lying on the front: two jumps | passed |
| Standing, folding, standing, folding: back and forth once too often | passed |
| Folding and coming back up once is a movement, not back and forth | passed |
| The same pose twice in a row repeats | passed |
| Every way between levels goes both ways | passed |
| Between two poses a way joins, at most one foot steps far: the body never jumps | passed |
| Between two poses a way joins, the body stays on the floor: never floating, never under it deeper than a step may sink | passed |

<a id="Spoken"></a>

### How long words take to say

`Spoken` · `src/content.ts:70` · status: **held**

The seconds a voice takes to say a text, at the rate voices speak, with the breath word before it or not.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
({ rate, counts }) => (text: string, withBreath: boolean): number =>
    counts.count(text) / rate.charactersPerSecond + (withBreath ? rate.breathWord : counts.zero)
```

</details>

- Owner: ghalaax

<a id="LevelWays"></a>

### The ways between levels

`LevelWays` · `src/content.ts:37`

From each level, the levels a body reaches in one movement, one foot stepping at a time: from standing it folds forward; folded, it steps one leg back into a lunge; from a lunge, a plank or a dog; from a plank it lowers to the floor, comes onto its knees, or lifts its hips into a dog; lying on its front, it pushes back into a plank or a dog; kneeling, it comes onto all fours or into a dog; on all fours, into a dog or a plank. The ways go both ways, and each keeps the body on the floor as the engine moves it (a criterion of "A sequence that makes sense").

| Level | Value |
|---|---|
| standing | fold |
| fold | standing, lunge |
| lunge | fold, plank, dog |
| plank | lunge, prone, dog, allFours |
| dog | lunge, plank, prone, kneeling, allFours |
| prone | plank, dog |
| kneeling | dog, allFours |
| allFours | plank, dog, kneeling |

- Decided by: ghalaax
- Rejected: Any pose after any other, standing, lying, standing, kneeling: a body cannot go that way, and the mannequin would pass through the floor; From lying on the front straight back onto the heels, the engine swings the thighs under the floor (20 cm deep) on the way to the child's pose; From the forward bend straight back into a dog, and back, both feet step back at once: the body would jump, held on its hands
- Used by: [A sequence drawn by lot](composing.md#DrawnSequence), [A sequence that makes sense](#MakesSense)
- Used by: [Criteria of a sequence that makes sense](#MakesSenseCriteria)
